chunks: And from Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Sahl ibn Hammad (Abu Itab al-Dallal) narrated to us, who said: Yunus ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated to us, who said: Awl ibn Abi Jahimah narrated to us, from his father, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while he was delivering a sermon, and my uncle was sitting in front of him.
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The affair of my nation will remain sound until twelve caliphs have passed, all of them from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number of caliphs from Quraysh?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Al-Nu'mani, establishes the number and tribal origin of the twelve leaders as a divine guarantee for the community's spiritual integrity. In Shia scholarship, it is interpreted not merely as a political prediction but as a theological mandate linking the twelve caliphs directly to the twelve Imams, emphasizing their Qurayshi lineage as a sign of legitimacy. The narration underscores the continuity of divine guidance through these specific figures until the end of the era of political caliphate.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (24) Abdul Wahab bin Abdul Majeed narrated tradition from Dawood from his father from ash-Shi’bi from Samra bin Jundub from the Prophet (S). (The same tradition narrated by Anass bin Malik that we have mentioned at the beginning of this chapter; tradition no.6).
